mainTopic: Food status by intent (the crow and the פטר חמור), whether רבי שמעון forbids a פטר חמור after עריפה, and the minimum value for redeeming it
overview: The amud begins by explaining a dispute about a slaughtered פטר חמור: the case is one where it was slaughtered only to practice שחיטה. The גמרא links this to the dispute between נימוס and רבי אליעזר about a crow slaughtered for practice. It reads that dispute as being about איסורו חישובו, but then suggests רבי אליעזר may rely only on the crow's סימני טהרה. Next, the גמרא challenges רבה, who says even רבי שמעון forbids a פטר חמור after עריפה. It answers that the ברייתא's dispute concerns only a live donkey, both for benefit from its value and from its body. רב נחמן supports רבה with two proofs, one from עגלה ערופה and one from לוי's ברייתא, but both are deflected. ריש לקיש agrees with רבה, while רבי יוחנן (or רבי אלעזר) holds the dispute continues after עריפה. The גמרא then discusses the משנה that קידושין with a פטר חמור does not work, explaining it through רבי יוסי בר יהודה's rule that redemption needs at least a שקל, which רבא derives from the ערכין verse. The amud ends as the גמרא begins to explain how the רבנן use that verse, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The case is slaughtering only to practice
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that the case under discussion is one where the animal was slaughtered only to practice שחיטה. It links the dispute to the argument between נימוס and רבי אליעזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: What case are we dealing with here? A case where he slaughtered it to practice on it. They disagree about the same issue that נימוס and רבי אליעזר argue about.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question on the previous amud by narrowing the case: the person slaughtered the animal only to practice, not to eat it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If someone slaughters an animal to eat it, he clearly treats it as food. If he slaughters it only to practice, there is no such intent. So the question becomes whether the animal's being forbidden (איסור) can stand in for that missing intent. The גמרא says this is the very point that נימוס and רבי אליעזר argue about.

keyTerms.meaning: Here, what case are we dealing with? (a formula that narrows the case)
To practice on it (to learn how to slaughter)
A dispute
A תנא, the brother of רבי יהושע הגרסי

steps.whyThisMatters: This step moves the whole discussion from a case about a firstborn donkey to a general principle about intent and food status. That principle is then tested on the crow.

phrases.english: Here, with what are we dealing?
phrases.notes: A standard answer formula that limits the case to a specific situation.

phrases.english: For example, where he slaughtered it to practice on it,

steps.terutzMaskana: The case is slaughter only for practice, where the only possible 'food intent' would come from the animal's prohibition.

steps.title: The ברייתא about slaughtering a crow for practice
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא. In it, נימוס rules that the blood of a crow slaughtered for practice is מכשיר. רבי אליעזר says that blood of שחיטה is always מכשיר.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: רבי יוסי said, נימוס, the brother of רבי יהושע הגרסי, told me that if someone slaughters a crow to practice on it, its blood makes food able to become impure. רבי אליעזר says: blood of slaughter always makes food able to become impure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the source text of the dispute between נימוס and רבי אליעזר that it just mentioned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Food can only become טמא after it has been wet by one of seven special liquids. This is called הכשר, and blood is one of those liquids. נימוס says the blood of a crow slaughtered for practice still counts as such a liquid. רבי אליעזר says the blood of any שחיטה always counts.

keyTerms.meaning: As it was taught in a ברייתא
He told me
A crow (a non-kosher bird)
Makes food able to become טמא (gives it הכשר)
Blood that comes out during slaughter

steps.confusionAlert: Here מכשיר does NOT mean 'makes kosher.' It means the blood makes other food able to receive טומאה.

phrases.english: As it was taught: Rabbi Yosei said:
Nimos told me,
the brother of Rabbi Yehoshua HaGarsi,
that one who slaughters a crow to practice on it —

phrases.notes: Blood is one of the seven liquids that can give הכשר.

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer says:
Blood of slaughter always renders food susceptible.
phrases.notes: On the surface, this sounds the same as נימוס. The next step asks about that.

steps.raayaObject: That there is a known dispute about an animal slaughtered for practice
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of רבי יוסי quoting נימוס, and the response of רבי אליעזר

steps.title: רבי אליעזר seems to say the same as the תנא קמא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that רבי אליעזר's statement seems identical to what נימוס said.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר is the same as the תנא קמא!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a problem with the ברייתא. Both opinions seem to say the blood is מכשיר, so what are they arguing about?
steps.deeperAnalysis: A ברייתא would not record two opinions if they meant exactly the same thing. Since both say the blood counts as a liquid that gives הכשר, there must be a hidden difference between them. This challenge sets up the answer in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: That is the same as
The first (unnamed or first-cited) opinion; here, נימוס

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer is the same as the first tanna!
phrases.notes: Both seem to hold that the blood is מכשיר.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ברייתא quoted in step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: The two opinions in the ברייתא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Two opinions that say the same thing cannot be a real dispute, so the difference between them must be identified.

steps.title: They argue about whether a prohibition counts as intent
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the real difference between them is איסורו חישובו: whether the crow's prohibition counts as intent to treat it as food.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, isn't it that the difference between them is whether its prohibition counts as its intent?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא identifies the hidden point of disagreement between נימוס and רבי אליעזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Something people do not normally eat, like a crow, is only treated as 'food' for טומאה if someone intends it as food. The question is whether the Torah's prohibition on eating it already gives it food status, as if the Torah 'thought' of it as food. The two opinions argue about this, not about the blood.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, isn't it that... (introduces the proposed answer)
Its prohibition counts as its intent (to treat it as food)
There is a difference between them

steps.whatToRemember: The dispute between נימוס and רבי אליעזר is really about איסורו חישובו: does a food's being forbidden give it food status without anyone's intent?
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the principle that step 1 applies to the firstborn donkey slaughtered for practice.

phrases.english: Rather, isn't it that whether its prohibition is its intent
phrases.notes: Does the prohibition count as 'thinking of it' as food?

phrases.english: is the difference between them?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא לָאו אִיסּוּרוֹ חִישּׁוּבוֹ אִיכָּא בֵּינַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the קשיא of step 3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifying a hidden practical difference (איכא בינייהו)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both opinions seemed identical, since both say the blood is מכשיר.
steps.terutzMaskana: They differ on whether the crow's prohibition counts as intent to treat it as food.

steps.title: The תנא קמא's view: the crow itself needs real intent
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that according to the תנא קמא, the crow's blood is מכשיר for other foods, but the crow itself needs real intent to count as food.
steps.simpleTranslation: The תנא קמא holds: its blood makes food in general able to become impure, but to make the crow itself food, intent is needed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא spells out the opinion of the תנא קמא (נימוס) to show how it differs from רבי אליעזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For נימוס, the blood works as a liquid that gives הכשר to other foods. However, the crow's meat does not become 'food' for טומאה just because it is forbidden; it needs actual intent. So נימוס holds the prohibition does NOT count as intent. By contrast, רבי אליעזר's word 'always' implies that the prohibition does count.

keyTerms.meaning: For everything else in general (other foods)
For itself (the crow's own body)
Intent to treat it as food

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two effects. One is the blood making OTHER foods able to become impure. The other is the crow's OWN meat counting as food. נימוס says yes to the first and requires intent for the second.

phrases.english: The first tanna holds:
its blood renders other foods in general susceptible,
but for itself, intent is required.
phrases.notes: People do not normally eat crows, so its prohibition alone does not make it food.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Expands the answer of step 4 by explaining the תנא קמא's side of the dispute.
steps.terutzMaskana: The תנא קמא holds that איסורו אינו חישובו (the prohibition does not count as intent), so the crow itself needs real intent.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר's position spelled out
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes its answer. רבי אליעזר holds that the blood of שחיטה is always מכשיר, and even the crow itself needs no intent to count as food.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי אליעזר comes to say: the blood of slaughter always makes things able to become impure, and even for the crow itself, no intent is needed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the answer from Step 5 by explaining what רבי אליעזר adds beyond the תנא קמא (נימוס).
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא said the crow's blood is מכשיר for other foods, but the crow's own meat needs real intent before it counts as food. רבי אליעזר goes further: the crow's own meat also counts as food with no intent, because its איסור (being forbidden) itself counts as intent. This is the practical difference behind איסורו חישובו.

keyTerms.meaning: The blood that comes out when an animal is slaughtered
For itself, meaning the animal's own meat
Intent, here intent to treat something as food
Always, in every case

steps.whyThisMatters: This finishes the explanation of how רבי אליעזר differs from נימוס. That difference is the basis for linking this argument to the dispute about the פטר חמור.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Eliezer comes to say:
phrases.notes: Shows what רבי אליעזר adds beyond the first opinion.

phrases.english: the blood of slaughter always makes things able to become impure,
and even for the crow itself as well
phrases.notes: This is the new point: the crow's own meat.

phrases.english: intent is not needed.
phrases.notes: Because its איסור counts as intent.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Defining each side of the dispute
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי אליעזר seemed to say exactly what נימוס said.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי אליעזר adds that even the crow's own meat needs no intent, since its איסור counts as intent.

steps.title: Maybe a crow is special because it has signs of a kosher bird
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions the link. Maybe רבי אליעזר's reason is not איסורו חישובו at all. Maybe it is that a crow has some סימני טהרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do you know this? Maybe רבי אליעזר's reason there is that a crow is different, since it has some signs of a kosher bird.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the idea from Step 1 that the פטר חמור dispute is the same as the crow dispute.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If רבי אליעזר rules this way only because the crow has some סימני טהרה, then his rule teaches nothing about a donkey. A donkey has no kosher signs. So the link between the two disputes falls apart.

keyTerms.meaning: From where? How do you know?
Maybe, perhaps
Is different
Signs of a kosher (pure) animal or bird

steps.confusionAlert: The crow is still a non-kosher bird. The point is only that it has SOME kosher signs, and that is enough to make it count as food more easily.

phrases.english: From where do you know this?
Perhaps the reason of Rabbi Eliezer there
phrases.notes: Offers a different reason for his ruling.

phrases.english: is that a crow is different,
since it has signs of a kosher bird.
phrases.notes: A donkey has no such signs, so the comparison fails.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the whole link built in Steps 1-6 by giving a different reason for רבי אליעזר.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The link between the פטר חמור dispute and the נימוס / רבי אליעזר dispute.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רבי אליעזר's ruling may depend on the crow's סימני טהרה, which a donkey lacks.

steps.title: Proof that kosher signs really matter
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא supports the new idea. It shows from רבי שמעון that סימני טהרה make a difference for food impurity.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how do we know that kosher signs are a meaningful thing? Because a ברייתא teaches about that משנה: רבי שמעון said, what is the reason? Since they have kosher signs.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a source to show that the idea in Step 7 is real and not made up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה on 10a lists animals like the camel, hare, and pig whose meat can become impure as food with no extra conditions. רבי שמעון explains why: they have some סימני טהרה. So kosher signs really can make an animal count as food. That makes the crow explanation strong.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know?
It is a real, meaningful factor
It is taught about it (a ברייתא on that משנה)
What is the reason?

phrases.english: And from where do we know that kosher signs are a meaningful factor?
As it is taught about that משנה,
phrases.notes: Refers to the משנה on 10a about the camel, hare, rock-badger, and pig.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon said: What is the reason?
Since they have signs of kosher animals.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Backs up the דחיה of Step 7 with a source.
steps.raayaObject: That סימני טהרה are a real factor that makes an animal count as food for impurity.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא on the משנה of 10a, where רבי שמעון explains the rule about the camel, hare, rock-badger, and pig.

steps.title: Then why talk about slaughtering for practice?
steps.stepSummary: A problem with the new idea: if kosher signs are the reason, the 'practice' case should not matter. Even a careless slaughter should be enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you will say: if the reason is kosher signs, why speak specifically about slaughtering to practice? Even if he slaughtered without paying attention, it should also count!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a possible objection to the kosher-signs explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the crow counts as food only because of its kosher signs, then intent should not matter at all. So why does the ברייתא describe a crow slaughtered 'to practice'? Even one slaughtered with no attention (מתעסק) should count, according to רבי אליעזר.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you will say (introduces a possible objection)
Why specifically this case?
To practice or learn how to slaughter
Acting without attention or purpose (מתעסק)

phrases.english: And if you will say:
if it is because of kosher signs,
why specifically the case of slaughtering to practice?
Even if he acted without attention, it should also count!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא: אִי מִשּׁוּם סִימָנֵי טׇהֳרָה, מַאי אִירְיָא לְהִתְלַמֵּד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the kosher-signs explanation from Steps 7-8.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רבי אליעזר's reason is the crow's סימני טהרה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If kosher signs alone make the crow food, the detail 'slaughtered to practice' adds nothing. Even a careless slaughter should be enough.

steps.title: Yes, and the case was chosen because of נימוס
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא agrees that for רבי אליעזר even a careless slaughter would count. The 'practice' case was used only because of נימוס's view.
steps.simpleTranslation: Yes, that is indeed so. And the case was stated because of נימוס.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the objection and keeps the kosher-signs explanation alive.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי אליעזר, the crow would count as food even if slaughtered with no attention. The ברייתא used the 'practice' case only because נימוס holds something strong: even a purposeful slaughter, if done just for practice, does not make it food. So the crow dispute may be about kosher signs, and it cannot prove anything about the פטר חמור.

keyTerms.meaning: Yes, that is indeed so
And because of

steps.whatToRemember: The attempt to link the פטר חמור dispute to נימוס and רבי אליעזר is weakened. רבי אליעזר may rule the crow is food only because it has סימני טהרה, which a donkey does not have.

phrases.english: Yes, that is indeed so,
phrases.notes: For רבי אליעזר, even a careless slaughter would count.

phrases.english: and the case was stated because of Nimos.
phrases.notes: נימוס says even a purposeful slaughter for practice does not make it food.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 9 by accepting it and explaining the choice of case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Accepting the point and explaining why the case was chosen
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Mentioning 'to practice' suggests the kosher-signs reason cannot be right.
steps.terutzMaskana: For רבי אליעזר even a careless slaughter would count. The practice case was used to show how far נימוס goes.

steps.title: A teaching that seems to contradict רבה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבה with a ברייתא. In it, רבי יהודה forbids benefit from a פטר חמור whose neck was broken, and רבי שמעון permits it.
steps.simpleTranslation: He raised an objection to him: If the owner does not want to redeem the firstborn donkey, he breaks its neck from behind with a cleaver and buries it, and it is forbidden for benefit. These are the words of רבי יהודה. רבי שמעון permits it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא to attack רבה. רבה had said that even רבי שמעון forbids benefit from the donkey after its neck is broken.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא first describes breaking the neck and burying the donkey. Then it says 'forbidden for benefit', and רבי שמעון argues and permits. This sounds like רבי שמעון permits benefit even after the neck is broken, which is the opposite of what רבה said.

keyTerms.meaning: He raised an objection to him (from a ברייתא)
A firstborn male donkey, which must be redeemed with a lamb or have its neck broken
Breaking the neck (the Torah's alternative to redeeming the donkey)
A cleaver, a heavy chopping knife
Forbidden to get any benefit from it

phrases.english: He raised an objection to him:
phrases.notes: The challenge is aimed at רבה

phrases.english: If he did not want to redeem it —
phrases.notes: The firstborn donkey, which is normally redeemed with a lamb

steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's claim that even רבי שמעון forbids benefit from a פטר חמור after עריפה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא mentions the breaking and burial, then records רבי שמעון as permitting benefit. This suggests he permits it even after death.

steps.title: Read the teaching as talking about a live donkey
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reinterprets the ברייתא. The argument is about benefit while the donkey is still alive, not after its neck is broken.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say it means: while it is still alive it is forbidden for benefit, and רבי שמעון permits.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבה by reading the ברייתא differently. The disagreement is only about a live donkey.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With this reading, רבי שמעון only permits benefit while the donkey is alive. He could still agree with רבה that once the neck is broken, the donkey is forbidden. So the ברייתא no longer contradicts רבה.

keyTerms.meaning: Say (read the text this way)
While it is still alive
Permits

phrases.english: Say: and while alive it is forbidden for benefit,
phrases.notes: A new reading of the ברייתא

phrases.english: and Rabbi Shimon permits.
phrases.notes: He permits only while it is alive

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 11 by changing how we read the ברייתא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation of the ברייתא's case (alive, not after death)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא's argument was about the donkey after its neck was broken.
steps.terutzMaskana: The argument is about a live donkey, so רבי שמעון may agree with רבה about a dead one.

steps.title: The last clause already covers a live donkey
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the new reading. The ברייתא's last clause deals with a live donkey, so the first clause must deal with a dead one.
steps.simpleTranslation: But since the last clause is about a live donkey, the first clause is not about a live donkey.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer from step 12. It says the 'alive' case is already covered later in the same ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A ברייתא would not teach the same case twice. If the last part is about a live donkey, the first part must be about something else: a donkey after its neck is broken. That puts us back to the original problem for רבה.

keyTerms.meaning: But look, surely (introduces a pushback)
The last clause of a teaching
The first clause of a teaching

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two clauses. The first clause (רישא) is now understood to be about the donkey after death. The last clause (סיפא) is about the donkey while alive.

steps.kashyaTarget: The reading in step 12 that the first clause is about a live donkey
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The last clause already handles the live donkey. So the first clause cannot repeat that case and must be about a donkey after death.

steps.title: Quoting the last clause to show it is about a live donkey
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא's last clause. It forbids improper ways of killing the donkey and forbids shearing and working it, which only applies while it is alive.
steps.simpleTranslation: As the last clause teaches: He may not kill it with a reed, a sickle, an ax, or a saw. Nor may he put it in a room and lock the door in front of it so that it dies. It is forbidden to shear it or work with it. These are the words of רבי יהודה. רבי שמעון permits.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the actual words of the last clause. This proves the claim in step 13 that it deals with a live donkey.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The last clause first lists wrong ways to kill the donkey, since the Torah requires breaking its neck. It then forbids shearing and labor, which can only happen while the donkey is alive. So the 'alive' argument is already here, and the first clause must be about after death, as step 13 said.

phrases.notes: This only applies to a live animal

phrases.english: these are the words of Rabbi Yehuda,
and Rabbi Shimon permits!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the text that proves the claim in step 13.
steps.raayaObject: That the סיפא of the ברייתא deals with a live donkey, so the רישא must deal with a dead one
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא's סיפא, which forbids shearing and labor (only possible while the donkey is alive)

steps.title: Both clauses deal with a live donkey, but with different kinds of benefit
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers the challenge. Both the רישא and the סיפא of the ברייתא deal with a live donkey. The רישא is about benefit from its value, and the סיפא is about benefit from its body.
steps.simpleTranslation: The first clause and the last clause both deal with the donkey while it is alive. The first clause is about benefit from its value, and the last clause is about benefit from its body.
steps.whatsHappening: The challenge was that if the סיפא deals with a live donkey, the רישא must deal with a dead one. The גמרא answers that both clauses deal with a live donkey, just with two different kinds of benefit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge assumed the two clauses could not both be about a live animal, since that would be repetitive. The גמרא shows they are not repetitive. One clause is about using the donkey's money value, such as selling or renting it. The other is about using the donkey's body directly, such as shearing it or making it work. So רבה's reading still stands: the dispute is only while the donkey is alive.

keyTerms.meaning: The first clause of a source
The last clause of a source
While it is alive
Benefit from its value (selling or renting it)
Benefit from its body (shearing it or working it)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the רישא is now about a dead donkey. The point of this answer is that neither clause is about a dead donkey. Both are about a live one.

phrases.english: The first clause and the last clause are both while it is alive,
the first clause is about benefit from its value,
phrases.notes: For example, selling or renting the donkey

phrases.english: the last clause is about benefit from its body.
phrases.notes: For example, shearing it or working with it

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of steps 13 and 14, which said the רישא must deal with a dead donkey.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-division of the clauses: same state (alive), different kinds of benefit.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the סיפא deals with a live donkey, the רישא must deal with a dead one.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both clauses deal with a live donkey. The רישא is about benefit from its value and the סיפא is about benefit from its body.

steps.title: Why the dispute had to be taught in both cases
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains why the ברייתא needed to state the argument for both value-benefit and body-benefit. From either case alone, we might have wrongly guessed the opinions in the other case.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was necessary to teach both. If the ברייתא had taught only benefit from its value, I would say that only in that case does רבי שמעון permit, but for benefit from its body he agrees with רבי יהודה that it is forbidden. And if it had taught only benefit from its body, I would say that only in that case does רבי יהודה forbid, but for benefit from its value he agrees with רבי שמעון that it is permitted. So both were necessary.
steps.whatsHappening: Someone might ask why the ברייתא repeats the same argument twice. The גמרא answers that each case teaches something we could not have learned from the other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Benefit from value is a lighter kind of use, so רבי שמעון's leniency there would not show he is lenient for body-benefit too. Body-benefit is a stronger kind of use, so רבי יהודה's strictness there would not show he is strict for value-benefit too. Teaching both cases shows that each רבי holds his opinion fully in both.

keyTerms.meaning: It is necessary (to teach both cases)
If [the תנא] had taught
I would say (a mistaken assumption)
Agrees, concedes
Permits / forbids

steps.whyThisMatters: This makes the answer in step 15 stronger. The two clauses are not just different. Each one is needed, so the ברייתא is not repeating itself.

phrases.english: And it is necessary [to teach both],
for if it had taught only benefit from its value,
[I would say] in that case Rabbi Shimon permits,
but regarding benefit from its body,
I would say he agrees with Rabbi Yehuda [that it is forbidden].
And if it had taught only benefit from its body,
[I would say] in that case Rabbi Yehuda forbids,
but regarding benefit from its value,
I would say he agrees with Rabbi Shimon [that it is permitted].
[Therefore] it is necessary.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports step 15 by explaining why two separate clauses about a live donkey are not redundant.
steps.terutzResolutionType: צריכותא: each case is needed so we do not wrongly limit either opinion.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: From one case alone, we might think רבי שמעון permits only value-benefit, or that רבי יהודה forbids only body-benefit.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון hold their opinions in both kinds of benefit.

steps.title: רב נחמן supports רבה: after the neck is broken, everyone forbids
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן, quoting רבה בר אבוה, says that even רבי שמעון agrees the donkey is forbidden after עריפה. This matches רבה's view.
steps.simpleTranslation: And so said רב נחמן in the name of רבה בר אבוה: רבי שמעון agrees that after the neck is broken, it is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another אמורא who says the same thing as רבה. The argument is only while the donkey is alive, and after עריפה it is forbidden according to everyone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word וכן ("and so") tells us this statement supports the view the גמרא has been defending. רבי שמעון, the lenient one, admits that once the neck is broken no benefit is allowed. This fits the reading that the ברייתא's dispute is only about a live donkey.

keyTerms.meaning: And so said (introduces support for a view)
Breaking the neck
Firstborn donkey
Forbidden (here: forbidden for benefit)

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the position of רבה and רב נחמן: after עריפה, even רבי שמעון forbids the donkey. It is not unanimous. רבי יוחנן (or רבי אלעזר) later says the dispute continues even after עריפה (Step 27).

phrases.english: And so said Rav Nachman,
[quoting what] Rabba bar Avuh said:
Rabbi Shimon agrees that after the neck is broken
it is forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכֵן אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After defending רבה's reading of the ברייתא, the גמרא brings an אמורא who agrees with רבה.
steps.raayaObject: רבה's position that the dispute is only while the donkey is alive, and that after עריפה it is forbidden according to all.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The statement of רב נחמן in the name of רבה בר אבוה.

steps.title: The source: a word-link to עגלה ערופה
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן shows his source. The word עריפה is used both for the פטר חמור and for the עגלה ערופה. Just as the עגלה ערופה is forbidden for benefit, so is the פטר חמור after its neck is broken.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב נחמן said: From where do I say this? As a ברייתא teaches about the verse "and you shall break its neck": breaking the neck is said here, and breaking the neck is said there [by עגלה ערופה]. Just as there it is forbidden, so too here it is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן proves his ruling from a ברייתא that uses a גזירה שוה, a link between two places in the Torah that use the same word.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah uses the word for breaking the neck both for the firstborn donkey and for the calf in the עגלה ערופה ceremony. The calf is forbidden for benefit after its neck is broken. Because the same word is used, the same rule carries over to the donkey. This gives a source in the Torah for the ruling in step 17.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do I say it? (asking for a source)
As it was taught in a ברייתא
A link between two passages based on the same word
The calf whose neck is broken for an unsolved murder
Here / there (the two places being compared)

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבה and רב נחמן, the dispute between רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון is only about a live פטר חמור, both for benefit from its value and from its body. רב נחמן tries to prove that after עריפה even רבי שמעון forbids it, using the shared word עריפה with עגלה ערופה. Step 20 shows this proof can be deflected, and step 27 brings רבי יוחנן, who holds the dispute continues even after עריפה.
steps.confusionAlert: The verse "וערפתו" is about the donkey ("here"). "There" (להלן) means עגלה ערופה. The prohibition goes from the calf to the donkey, not the other way around.

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַב נַחְמָן: מְנָא אָמֵינָא לַהּ?
phrases.english: And Rav Nachman said: From where do I say this?
As it was taught: "And you shall break its neck" (Exodus 13:13),
breaking the neck is said here,
and breaking the neck is said there,
phrases.notes: Referring to עגלה ערופה (Deuteronomy 21:4)

phrases.english: just as there it is forbidden,
so too here it is forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַב נַחְמָן: מְנָא אָמֵינָא לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the Torah source for רב נחמן's ruling in step 17.
steps.raayaObject: That a פטר חמור is forbidden for benefit after עריפה, even according to רבי שמעון.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא using a גזירה שוה of the word עריפה between פטר חמור and עגלה ערופה.

steps.title: The source must follow רבי שמעון, not רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which תנא is behind the עגלה ערופה derivation. It cannot be רבי יהודה, so it must be רבי שמעון.
steps.simpleTranslation: Who is this? If you say רבי יהודה, he already forbids the donkey while it is alive! So is it not רבי שמעון?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes רב נחמן's proof. It shows that the teaching about עריפה must come from רבי שמעון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה already forbids benefit from the פטר חמור while it is alive. For him, a verse saying it is forbidden after עריפה would teach nothing new. So the teaching must belong to רבי שמעון, who permits the donkey while it is alive. This shows that רבי שמעון agrees it becomes forbidden after עריפה.

keyTerms.meaning: Who is it? (Which תנא said this?)
If you say
While still alive
Rather, is it not…?

phrases.english: Who is this? If you say it is Rabbi Yehuda —
he already forbids it while it is alive!
phrases.notes: So the עריפה teaching would be pointless for him.

phrases.english: Rather, is it not Rabbi Shimon?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Identifies the תנא behind the עגלה ערופה derivation from Step 18.
steps.raayaObject: Even רבי שמעון forbids the פטר חמור after עריפה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The word-link between פטר חמור and עגלה ערופה, which only adds something new according to רבי שמעון.

steps.title: רב ששת: the source can still follow רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת quotes ספרא. The teaching can follow רבי יהודה, because it is needed to block the idea that עריפה permits the donkey the way פדיה does.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת said to him: Your colleague ספרא explained it this way. Really, it is רבי יהודה, and the teaching was needed. You might have thought that breaking the neck stands in place of redeeming. Just as redeeming permits the donkey, breaking its neck would permit it too. So the teaching tells us it does not.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת pushes back on the proof from Step 19. He shows that the teaching can fit רבי יהודה after all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof depended on the claim that the teaching adds nothing for רבי יהודה. רב ששת shows it does add something. The Torah presents עריפה as the alternative to פדיה, so we might think it also permits the donkey, just as פדיה does. The teaching rules out that mistake, so it no longer has to belong to רבי שמעון.

keyTerms.meaning: Explained it
Really / actually (keeping the original position)
You might have thought
Redemption (of the פטר חמור with a lamb)
It teaches us (that the mistaken thought is wrong)

steps.confusionAlert: רב ששת does not say that רבי שמעון permits the donkey after עריפה. He only shows that this source does not prove that he forbids it.

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet said to him:
Safra, your colleague, explained it:
Actually it is Rabbi Yehuda, and it was necessary,
because it would enter your mind to say:
breaking the neck stands in place of redemption,
just as redemption permits —
so too breaking the neck permits,
so it teaches us otherwise.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב שֵׁשֶׁת: סָפְרָא חַבְרָיךְ תַּרְגּוּמַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof in Step 19 by showing the source can fit רבי יהודה.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof. רב נחמן's position itself is not disproven.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed the teaching is useless for רבי יהודה. In fact it blocks a possible comparison between עריפה and פדיה.

steps.title: רב נחמן brings a second source from the ברייתא of לוי
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן cites לוי's ברייתא: the owner caused the כהן to lose money, so he must lose his own money.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said: From where do I say this? From what לוי taught: He caused the כהן to lose money, therefore his own money shall be lost.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן offers a new source for his position. This step sets up the next step, which will identify whose opinion it follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: לוי explains the reason for עריפה as a penalty. The owner did not redeem the donkey and give the lamb to the כהן, so he loses the donkey's value. This sets up an argument about who could hold such a reason.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do I say this?
לוי taught (in a ברייתא)
Caused a loss of his money
Therefore

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן: מְנָא אָמֵינָא לַהּ?
phrases.english: Rav Nachman said: From where do I say it?
From what Levi taught:
He caused a loss of the priest's money,
therefore his own money shall be lost.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן: מְנָא אָמֵינָא לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the first proof was rejected in Step 20, רב נחמן brings a new source.
steps.raayaObject: Even רבי שמעון forbids the פטר חמור after עריפה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of לוי, which explains עריפה as a monetary penalty.

steps.title: לוי's ברייתא must follow רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: For רבי יהודה, the money is already lost while the donkey is alive. So the penalty idea only works for רבי שמעון.
steps.simpleTranslation: Who is this? If you say רבי יהודה, the money is already lost! So is it not רבי שמעון?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא identifies the תנא behind לוי's ברייתא. It concludes that the ברייתא follows רבי שמעון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יהודה, the donkey is forbidden while alive, so the owner has already lost its value. עריפה would cause no new loss. Only for רבי שמעון does עריפה turn a usable donkey into a forbidden one. That shows רבי שמעון holds it becomes forbidden after עריפה.

keyTerms.meaning: It already stands lost

steps.whatToRemember: רב נחמן's second proof: לוי says עריפה makes the owner lose his money. That only makes sense for רבי שמעון, so even רבי שמעון forbids the donkey after עריפה.

phrases.english: Who is this? If you say it is Rabbi Yehuda —
it already stands lost!
phrases.notes: For him, the donkey was forbidden while alive, so עריפה causes no new loss.

phrases.english: Rather, is it not Rabbi Shimon?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַנִּי? אִילֵימָא רַבִּי יְהוּדָה — הָא מַיפְסַד וְקָאֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the proof from לוי's ברייתא, introduced in Step 21.
steps.raayaObject: Even רבי שמעון forbids the פטר חמור after עריפה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The penalty reason in לוי's ברייתא only creates a new loss according to רבי שמעון.

steps.title: The teaching can fit either תנא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back on the proof from step 22. The בריתא about the owner losing money can follow רבי יהודה or רבי שמעון.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you want, say it follows רבי יהודה. And if you want, say it follows רבי שמעון.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the claim that לוי's בריתא only works for רבי שמעון. It says the בריתא can fit either תנא, and the next two lines explain how. This line sets up those explanations.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 22 argued that under רבי יהודה the money is already lost while the donkey is alive, so a 'penalty' makes no sense for him. The גמרא now says we can find a real loss under either view. If so, the בריתא no longer proves that רבי שמעון forbids the donkey after עריפה.

keyTerms.meaning: If you want, say (introduces one of two possible answers)
The תנא who forbids benefit from a פטר חמור even while it is alive
The תנא who permits benefit from a live פטר חמור

phrases.english: If you want, say: Rabbi Yehuda,
and if you want, say Rabbi Shimon.
phrases.notes: The two options are explained in the next two steps.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה, וְאִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects step 22's conclusion that the penalty idea works only for רבי שמעון.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from לוי's בריתא that רבי שמעון forbids benefit after עריפה
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed only one תנא could explain the loss. In fact a loss can be identified under both views.

steps.title: Under רבי יהודה the loss is the value gap
steps.stepSummary: Under רבי יהודה, the owner loses the difference between what the donkey is worth and what the cheaper lamb is worth.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you want, say it follows רבי יהודה. The loss is the difference in between.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how the בריתא can follow רבי יהודה. The owner's loss is the 'in-between' value.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יהודה, the unredeemed donkey is forbidden, so the owner cannot use it alive. But if he had redeemed it with a lamb, he would have gained a donkey worth more than the lamb he gave away. By breaking its neck instead, he loses that gain, and that is the penalty the בריתא means.

keyTerms.meaning: A loss
Of the in-between, meaning the difference in value
Redemption of the פטר חמור with a lamb

steps.confusionAlert: The loss is not the whole donkey. It is only the gap between the donkey's value and the lamb's value, which he would have kept by redeeming.

phrases.english: If you want, say: Rabbi Yehuda,
and the loss is of the difference in between.
phrases.notes: This is the donkey's value minus the lamb's value.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה, אַפְּסֵידָא דְּבֵינֵי בֵּינֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Fills in the first option offered in step 23.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining what 'loss' means in the בריתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Under רבי יהודה nothing is lost by עריפה, because the donkey was already forbidden.
steps.terutzMaskana: The owner still loses the extra value he would have gained by redeeming the donkey with a cheaper lamb.

steps.title: Under רבי שמעון the loss comes from the death
steps.stepSummary: Under רבי שמעון, even if the dead donkey is permitted, killing it lowers its value.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you want, say it follows רבי שמעון. The loss is the drop in value caused by death.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how the בריתא can follow רבי שמעון without assuming he forbids the donkey after עריפה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even if רבי שמעון permits benefit from the carcass, a dead donkey is worth much less than a live one. That drop in value is the owner's penalty. So the בריתא does not prove that רבי שמעון forbids the donkey after עריפה, and the proof for רב נחמן falls away.

keyTerms.meaning: A decrease in value
Death

steps.whatToRemember: לוי's בריתא proves nothing. Under רבי יהודה the loss is the value gap, and under רבי שמעון the loss is the drop in value from death.

phrases.english: And if you want, say: Rabbi Shimon,
and the loss refers to the drop in value from death.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן, לִפְחַת מִיתָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Fills in the second option offered in step 23 and completes the rejection of the proof.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Showing a loss exists even if the carcass is permitted
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The penalty must mean the carcass is forbidden, so רבי שמעון must forbid it after עריפה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The penalty can simply be the lower value of a dead animal, so nothing is proven about a prohibition.

steps.title: ריש לקיש agrees that רבי שמעון forbids after the neck-breaking
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש rules like רבה and רב נחמן: רבי שמעון agrees the donkey is forbidden after עריפה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And so said ריש לקיש: רבי שמעון agrees that after עריפה the donkey is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The proofs have been rejected, so the גמרא brings an אמורא who holds the same view as רבה and רב נחמן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase 'וכן אמר' means this אמורא says the same thing as the earlier position. ריש לקיש holds that the argument between רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון is only about the live donkey. Once its neck is broken, everyone agrees it is forbidden for benefit.

keyTerms.meaning: And so said (an אמורא agreeing with an earlier view)
An אמורא of ארץ ישראל, colleague of רבי יוחנן
Agrees, concedes
Breaking the animal's neck from behind

phrases.english: And so said Reish Lakish:
Rabbi Shimon concedes that after the neck-breaking
it is forbidden for benefit,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the textual proofs are rejected, the גמרא returns to the main question and cites an אמורא who agrees with רב נחמן.
steps.raayaObject: רבה and רב נחמן's claim that רבי שמעון forbids the donkey after עריפה

steps.title: רבי יוחנן holds the dispute continues after death
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן (some say רבי אלעזר) disagrees: רבי שמעון permits the donkey even after עריפה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוחנן, and some say רבי אלעזר, said: the dispute still exists.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the opposing view, which closes the discussion. This אמורא says רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון argue even after the neck is broken.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יוחנן, רבי שמעון never forbids the פטר חמור, alive or dead. So the question of what happens after עריפה depends on the original dispute, and it is not agreed by all. This leaves two clear sides: ריש לקיש with רבה and רב נחמן, against רבי יוחנן.

steps.title: Does the משנה go against רבי שמעון?
steps.stepSummary: Since רבי שמעון permits benefit from a פטר חמור, the משנה that invalidates the קידושין seems to disagree with him.

steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks whether this משנה goes against רבי שמעון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון holds that a פטר חמור may be used for benefit. If so, it has value, and a woman should be betrothed with it. The משנה says she is not betrothed, so it seems not to follow רבי שמעון.

steps.title: The משנה speaks of after the neck-breaking, and everyone agrees
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן in the name of רבה בר אבוה: the משנה is talking about after עריפה, when even רבי שמעון forbids the donkey.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said in the name of רבה בר אבוה: the משנה is talking about after the donkey's neck was broken, and so everyone agrees.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the משנה is talking about a donkey after עריפה. At that point even רבי שמעון agrees it is forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון permits the donkey only before עריפה. After עריפה it becomes forbidden for benefit according to everyone. So it has no value, and the קידושין fails even according to רבי שמעון.

steps.title: Another version: the משנה seems to fit neither רבי יהודה nor רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: Some say the question was different. The משנה fits neither רבי שמעון (she should be betrothed with the full value) nor רבי יהודה (she should be betrothed with the difference in value).
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say the discussion went like this: Whose view is this משנה? It fits neither רבי יהודה nor רבי שמעון. If it follows רבי שמעון, she should be betrothed with the whole value. If it follows רבי יהודה, she should be betrothed with the difference in between!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a different version of the question on the משנה. Now it seems to fit no one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון permits benefit, so the whole donkey counts as money. רבי יהודה requires giving a lamb to the כהן, but the owner keeps what the donkey is worth beyond the lamb, and that should be enough for קידושין. steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר אבוה said in the name of רב: Really, the משנה follows רבי יהודה. It is a case where the donkey is worth only a שקל, and he holds like רבי יוסי בר יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the משנה follows רבי יהודה. It is talking about a donkey worth only a שקל, so the owner keeps nothing of value.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי יוסי בר יהודה, the lamb given to the כהן must be worth at least a שקל. If the donkey itself is worth only a שקל, then the donkey's value minus the lamb's value is zero. So there is nothing to betroth with.

steps.title: The source for רבי יוסי בר יהודה's minimum of a שקל
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא: the doubled word 'תפדה' teaches that you redeem immediately and with any amount. רבי יוסי בר יהודה says a redemption cannot be less than a שקל.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: 'You shall redeem,' 'you shall redeem': redeem right away, and redeem with any amount. רבי יוסי בר יהודה says: no redemption may be less than a שקל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא as the source for רבי יוסי בר יהודה's view, which the last answer relied on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first תנא learns from the doubled word 'תפדה' that you may redeem immediately and with a lamb of any value. רבי יוסי בר יהודה disagrees and requires a minimum of a שקל. That minimum is what makes the answer in step 32 work.

steps.title: Why would we need a verse to teach this? It is obvious
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the first part of the ברייתא and asks: isn't it obvious that you can redeem immediately and with any amount?
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: 'You shall redeem,' 'you shall redeem': redeem right away, redeem with any amount. Isn't that obvious?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts to analyze the ברייתא. It asks why a פסוק is needed for something that seems obvious.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is no reason to think a redemption must wait, or that it needs a set value. So the double 'תפדה' seems to teach nothing new. The גמרא will need to explain what the extra teaching adds.

keyTerms.meaning: The Master said (quoting an earlier source to analyze it)

steps.confusionAlert: The quote is repeated on purpose. The גמרא is re-quoting the ברייתא in order to question it.

steps.title: Why the ברייתא had to teach 'immediately and any amount'
steps.stepSummary: The teaching was needed. Otherwise we might compare a firstborn donkey to a firstborn son, who is redeemed after thirty days and for five סלעים. The doubled word 'תפדה' teaches that the donkey is redeemed right away and with any amount.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was necessary. You might have thought: since the donkey is compared to a human firstborn, then just as a human firstborn is redeemed after thirty days and with five, this one too should be after thirty days and with five. So the verse teaches us: 'You shall redeem' means right away, and 'you shall redeem' means with any amount.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from Step 34. The teaching was not obvious, because there was a real reason to think otherwise.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse in במדבר mentions בכור אדם and the firstborn of an impure animal side by side. That closeness could suggest a היקש, which would copy the son's rules onto the donkey: wait thirty days and pay five סלעים. The doubled 'תפדה' blocks that comparison on both points, timing and amount.

steps.title: Where does רבי יוסי בר יהודה get a minimum of a שקל?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי יוסי בר יהודה's view that redemption cannot be less than a שקל and challenges it from both sides. With the היקש, the minimum should be five. Without it, there is no source for a שקל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי בר יהודה says: a redemption cannot be less than a שקל. Whichever way you look at it, there is a problem: if he compares it to a human firstborn, he should require five. And if he does not compare it, where does he get a שקל from?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the second half of the ברייתא and asks for רבי יוסי בר יהודה's source. It argues that his number does not fit either possible approach.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a ממה נפשך argument, which traps a position between two options. If he uses the היקש to בכור אדם, he should require the full five סלעים. If he rejects the היקש, he seems to have no reason for any minimum, so a שקל looks random.

steps.title: רבא: the שקל minimum comes from the verse about ערכין
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי בר יהודה does not use the היקש. רבא shows that his source is the verse 'וכל ערכך יהיה בשקל הקדש', which teaches that no valuation can be less than a שקל.
steps.simpleTranslation: Actually, he does not compare them. רבא said: the verse says, 'And all your valuations shall be with the שקל הקדש.' All valuations that you assess should not be less than a שקל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by choosing the second option: no היקש. It then gives a separate verse as the source for the שקל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The minimum does not come from comparing the donkey to a firstborn son. It comes from a general rule that any valuation for sacred purposes is at least a שקל. That explains why רבי יוסי בר יהודה requires a שקל and not five סלעים.

steps.title: What do the רבנן do with that verse?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא turns to the רבנן and begins to explain how they use the verse 'וכל ערכך יהיה בשקל הקדש', since they do not learn a one-שקל minimum from it.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the רבנן, who disagree with him, hold that that verse...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next move. It asks how the רבנן understand the verse that רבי יוסי בר יהודה used, and it starts the answer with 'that verse'. The rest of the answer comes in the next part of the text.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every verse in the תורה must teach something. If the רבנן do not learn a one-שקל minimum from 'וכל ערכך יהיה בשקל הקדש', the גמרא must show what the verse does teach in their view. The word 'ההוא' (that verse) tells us the גמרא is about to give the verse a different job.

keyTerms.meaning: The Rabbis. Here it means the majority view, the תנא קמא of the ברייתא, who say a firstborn donkey can be redeemed with any amount.
